Journal.Title: The New England Journal of Medicine

Article.ArticleTitle: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Duration in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome

Abstract.AbstractText: Guidelines recommend dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin and a P2Y12 inhibitor following acute coronary syndromes (ACS). However, the optimal duration balancing ischemic benefit against bleeding risk remains debated.
In a randomized multicenter trial, 4,000 patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for ACS were assigned to 3 months versus 12 months of DAPT followed by P2Y12 monotherapy.

At 12 months, major adverse cardiac events occurred in 4.2% of the 3-month cohort and 4.1% of the 12-month cohort (HR 1.02; 95% CI 0.81 to 1.30; p = 0.88). Major bleeding occurred in 1.1% versus 2.4% (HR 0.46; 95% CI 0.31 to 0.69; p < 0.001).
Shortened 3-month DAPT followed by P2Y12 monotherapy reduced major bleeding without increasing ischemic events in stabilized ACS patients.

Article.ArticleTitle: Empiric Antibiotic Regimens for Hospitalized Adults with Community-Acquired Pneumonia

Abstract.AbstractText: Among non-ICU inpatients with community-acquired pneumonia, beta-lactam monotherapy demonstrated non-inferiority to beta-lactam plus macrolide combination therapy with respect to 30-day all-cause clinical cure and in-hospital mortality.
